questions.question: Which of the following amines is most basic in aqueous medium?

options.explanation: Aniline is an aromatic amine and less basic in aqueous medium due to resonance stabilization of the lone pair on nitrogen.
Benzylamine is less basic than ethylamine due to resonance delocalization of the lone pair into the benzene ring.
Ethylamine is aliphatic and has a strong +I effect from the ethyl group, making it more basic than aromatic amines in aqueous medium.
p-Nitroaniline is less basic due to the electron-withdrawing nitro group, which reduces the availability of the lone pair on nitrogen.

questions.explanation: In aqueous medium, basicity is influenced by solvation and inductive effects. Ethylamine is aliphatic and has a strong +I effect from the ethyl group, making it more basic than aromatic amines like aniline or p-nitroaniline (due to electron-withdrawing nitro group). Benzylamine is less basic than ethylamine due to resonance delocalization of the lone pair into the benzene ring.
questions.hint: Consider the nature of the amine (aliphatic vs aromatic) and the presence of electron-withdrawing or donating groups.

questions.explanation: The Carbylamine reaction converts primary amines (both aliphatic and aromatic) into isocyanides (carbylamines) using chloroform and alcoholic KOH. Option A is incorrect because NaNO₂/HCl with Cu/HCl is used for the Sandmeyer reaction, producing aryl halides or phenols, not isocyanides. Option B (acylation) yields amides, and Option D (reduction) yields alkanes from nitriles.

questions.question: Arrange the following compounds in decreasing order of their basic strength: (i) Aniline, (ii) Ethylamine, (iii) p-Nitroaniline, (iv) Benzylamine

options.explanation: This order incorrectly places aniline before p-Nitroaniline, which is less basic due to the nitro group's electron-withdrawing effect.
This is the correct order based on the electron-donating and withdrawing effects on nitrogen.
This order incorrectly places benzylamine before ethylamine, which has a stronger +I effect.
This order incorrectly ranks p-Nitroaniline highest, which is the least basic due to the nitro group.

questions.explanation: Basic strength depends on electron density on nitrogen. Ethylamine (ii) is most basic due to +I effect of the ethyl group. Benzylamine (iv) is next due to resonance stabilization of the lone pair. p-Nitroaniline (iii) is less basic than aniline (i) because the nitro group withdraws electrons through resonance, reducing lone pair availability. Thus, the correct order is (ii) > (iv) > (iii) > (i).
questions.hint: Consider the electron-donating and electron-withdrawing effects on the nitrogen atom in these compounds.

questions.question: Aniline undergoes a reaction sequence: Aniline →[NaNO₂/HCl] A →[CuCN] B →[DIBAL-H] C. Identify the final product C.

Benzyl alcohol is not formed in this reaction sequence.

questions.explanation: Aniline undergoes diazotisation with NaNO₂/HCl to form benzenediazonium chloride (A). This reacts with CuCN in the Sandmeyer reaction to yield benzonitrile (B). Reduction of benzonitrile with DIBAL-H (diisobutylaluminium hydride) yields benzaldehyde (C). Options A, C, and D do not match this sequence.
questions.hint: Consider the intermediates formed in the Sandmeyer reaction and the reduction of nitriles.
questions.subject: neet-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the Hofmann bromamide reaction?

options.text: It involves the treatment of a primary amide with Br₂ and NaOH to yield a primary amine with one fewer carbon atom.
options.explanation: This is a correct statement about the Hofmann bromamide reaction.

options.text: The reaction proceeds via an isocyanate intermediate, which undergoes hydrolysis to form the amine.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect because the isocyanate is not a direct intermediate; the reaction proceeds via a bromamide intermediate that rearranges to an isocyanate.

options.text: The reaction is useful for the degradation of amides to amines.
options.explanation: This is a correct statement about the Hofmann bromamide reaction.

options.text: The reaction is not suitable for tertiary amides.
options.explanation: This is a correct statement because tertiary amides lack an N-H proton, preventing the reaction.

questions.explanation: The Hofmann bromamide reaction proceeds via a bromamide intermediate, which undergoes rearrangement to an isocyanate (not a direct intermediate), followed by hydrolysis to the amine. Thus, Option B is incorrect. Option A correctly describes the overall reaction, Option C is true, and Option D is correct because tertiary amides lack an N-H proton, preventing the reaction.
questions.hint: Focus on the mechanistic steps of the Hofmann bromamide reaction to identify the incorrect statement.
questions.subject: neet-chemistry
